interpretation: UPPER BOUND ON EXPOSURE, not a measurement of D&B sourcing. The definitive test in SAM.gov's terms is the EVS Source field, which is not present in USAspending award data, so this substitutes the earliest performance-period start across the transactions supporting each link. That proxy is deliberately over-inclusive: a task order placed in FY2025 against a long-running vehicle inherits the vehicle's original start date and is counted pre-cutoff even though the order itself is recent. Every transaction in this archive is FY2025, so under an action-date reading the exposure would be zero. The truth is between the two. We therefore publish the full benchmark, sourced from public-domain Treasury data, and also ship the post-cutoff subset for anyone needing the conservative position.

reconciliation_with_archive_parents.explanation: The two files count different objects. archive_parents.jsonl resolves each entity to a single parent by obligated-value plurality; this scan enumerates every distinct (child, parent) pair observed on any row. The delta decomposes into 372 extra pairs contributed by 358 entities that report more than one parent, and 369 entities whose plurality parent is themselves -- recorded as self-parent and therefore excluded from the aggregated genuine links -- but which name a different parent on some rows.
